finding.title: Archive or rewrite epic-19 sync stories 19-8/19-9 — both still target a SyncEngine/syncEngineProvider architecture that has been deleted
finding.rule: Tier-4 triage protocol (presents-as-current vs point-in-time); related AG-8/AG-9

evidence.quote: SUPERSEDED-ARCHITECTURE NOTE: This story's activation rule ("has Firebase account → activate") is from the March model.
W2.35: [syncEngineProvider] deleted — this is the sole write-path provider.

finding.why: These are the only two files in the batch still marked ready-for-dev, i.e. presented as live, pickable backlog rather than history. Both prescribe editing lib/features/sync/data/sync_engine.dart, making syncEngineProvider nullable, and adding SyncEngine.pushAllLocalData()/OfflineQueue.enqueue* calls. None of that exists anymore: SyncEngine, syncEngineProvider, and sync_engine.dart itself were deleted during the SyncOrchestrator+outbox rewrite (proven by the DNI-333/334/335 decomposition stories in this same batch and by the 'syncEngineProvider deleted' comment in sync_providers.dart) — the only remaining trace is a `.skip`-suffixed dead test file (test/features/sync/data/sync_engine_test.dart.skip). This repo runs an autonomous batch/worktree-per-story workflow (evidenced by the DNI-378..383 dev-agent records in this batch); a developer or agent that pulls '19-8' or '19-9' off the ready-for-dev backlog would burn a full worktree cycle trying to resurrect a provider that was deliberately deleted, risking a regression to the pre-outbox sync design. 19-8's own AC-3 goal (SyncStatus.localOnly) is already shipped via SyncOrchestrator, so the story is redundant as well as stale — only 19-8 carries a partial self-aware 'SUPERSEDED-ARCHITECTURE' note (and even that leaves Status at ready-for-dev); 19-9 carries no such warning at all.
finding.recommendation: Move 19-8 and 19-9 to docs/_archive/superseded/ (the repo already uses this location, e.g. docs/_archive/superseded/epic-15-stories/15.11-profile-scoped-providers-sync.md) with a pointer to what actually replaced them (DNI-333/334/335 SyncEngine decomp, DNI-342 tier threading, the SyncOrchestrator/outbox architecture) — or rewrite their ACs against SyncOrchestrator if the underlying user-facing goal is still open. Add a cheap Rule-0 doc-lint: for every docs/stories/implementation/*.md with Status in {ready-for-dev, backlog, todo}, grep the class/provider names listed under its 'File:' targets against lib/ and fail the audit if a named symbol doesn't resolve — this would have caught the drift immediately.
acceptance_criteria: 19-8 and 19-9 no longer sit at Status: ready-for-dev while referencing symbols (SyncEngine, syncEngineProvider) absent from lib/ — either archived/superseded-tagged or rewritten against SyncOrchestrator.
A grep-based checker (make audit target or tool/ script) flags any ready-for-dev/backlog story whose 'File:' targets don't exist in lib/, preventing silent recurrence.

finding.title: Backfill or formally waive verification evidence on epic-21 'done' stories — 16 files ship an all-unchecked task list and an empty Dev Agent Record
finding.why: All 16 epic-21 stories carry 'Status: done' yet every Tasks/Subtasks checkbox in every file is unchecked ('- [ ]', never '- [x]') and every Dev Agent Record section is the unfilled template stub (blank 'Agent Model Used' / 'Completion Notes List' / 'Change Log' headers, no content) — in sharp contrast to every DNI-32x/33x/34x/35x/37x/38x story in this same batch, which carries a populated file list, dated change log, and test-run counts (e.g. 'flutter test — 1810 passing'). Grepping lib/ shows the epic-21 feature set (device registry, per-account DB isolation, session persistence, account picker, tiered deletion, the onUserDeleted cloud function) genuinely exists, so the work itself was not skipped — but the documents supply no verifiable completion trail a reviewer or future incident investigator could check the 'done' claim against, unlike every other done/review story in the folder.
finding.recommendation: Not worth rewriting 16 historical files retroactively. Forward-looking fix: make the story-authoring skill (or a docs-triage Rule-0 checker) refuse Status: done/review when Tasks/Subtasks still contain an unchecked '- [ ]' line or the Dev Agent Record section is the unfilled template — this is exactly the discipline the later Epic-25+ process already adopted by convention; enforce it instead of leaving it as convention.
acceptance_criteria: A checker (doc-lint or make audit rule) fails when a docs/stories/implementation/*.md has Status: done/review and still contains an unchecked '- [ ]' line in Tasks/Subtasks, or a Dev Agent Record section with only empty headers.
New stories merged after this finding are not left with Status: done and a blank Dev Agent Record.
